summary: Mild autumn days in both cities, usually about 15–19° by day and 9–13° at night, with rain on some days, more often in Porto. Lisbon and Porto are hilly, so plan for a lot of walking up and down.

pack.why: November often has showers, more in Porto

pack.text: A warm layer for the evenings

know.title: Money
know.text: Euro. Cards work almost everywhere. Keep a few euros in coins for small cafés and markets.

know.title: Plugs
know.text: Type F, 230 V: the same as in the Netherlands. No adapter needed.

know.title: Tipping
know.text: Not expected. Round up, or leave about 5–10% for good service at a restaurant.

know.title: Couvert
know.text: Bread, olives or cheese that come to the table before you order are not free. If you do not want them, say "não, obrigado" and they go back.

know.title: Emergency
know.text: Call 112 for police, ambulance or fire.

know.title: A few words
know.text: Olá (hello) · Obrigado / Obrigada (thank you; a man / a woman says) · A conta, por favor (the bill, please).

know.title: Time
know.text: Portugal is 1 hour behind Amsterdam. Your flight times are local times.

know.title: ID
know.text: No passport control from Amsterdam (Schengen), but take your ID card or passport: airlines and hotels ask for it.

items.title: Airport to the centre
items.text: Take the metro red line from Aeroporto, about 20–30 min to the centre (change at Alameda, Saldanha or São Sebastião for other lines). Tap a contactless bank card at the gate (about €1.92 a ride), or buy a Navegante card (€0.50) and load credit (about €1.72 a ride). Tap in and tap out.

items.title: Trams and buses
items.text: Contactless cards work on Carris buses and most trams. On tram 28 a bank card costs about €3.30 a ride, but Navegante credit only about €1.72. Go early: tram 28 is very busy.

items.title: Train to Porto (Sunday)
items.text: Alfa Pendular from Santa Apolónia, about 3 hours. Every seat is reserved: your coach and seat are on the ticket. There are no ticket gates; find the platform on the departure board and get on before departure, because doors close about 1 minute before. The train stops at Lisboa Oriente about 9 minutes later.

items.title: Campanhã station to the centre
items.text: Take a local train from Campanhã to São Bento, in the old centre: about 4 minutes, every 5–15 minutes. Your Alfa Pendular ticket covers it within 1 hour of arrival. The Ribeira riverside is about 10 minutes' walk downhill from São Bento.

items.title: Metro and buses
items.text: Buy an Andante card (about €0.60) at a metro machine and load trips. Zone Z2 covers the centre (about €1.40 a ride). Tap the yellow validator before every ride, also when you change. Fines start at €50.

items.title: To the airport (Thursday)
items.text: Metro line E (violet) runs from Trindade to the airport in about 25–30 minutes; you need a Z4 ticket. For the 12:10 KLM flight, leave the centre by about 9:30.
